Cross validation for ctsem fits: K fold by refitting, or PSIS for Laplace fits

Source: R/ctLOO.R
ctLOO.Rd

Estimates out-of-sample predictive performance, by refitting the model with each fold of the data held out in turn or, for a julia Laplace fit, by Pareto smoothed importance sampling without refitting.

Usage

ctLOO(
  fit,
  folds = 10,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L),
  parallelFolds = FALSE,
  tol = NULL,
  subjectwise = ifelse(length(unique(.ctFitRowSubject(fit))) >= folds, TRUE, FALSE),
  keepfirstobs = FALSE,
  leaveOutN = NA,
  refit = TRUE,
  casewiseApproximation = FALSE,
  method = c("kfold", "psis"),
  nsamples = 1000
)

Arguments

fit

A fit from ctFit, on either backend.

folds

Number of cross validation splits to use – 10 folds implies that the model is re-fit 10 times, each time to a data set with 1/10 of the observations randomly removed.

cores

Number of processor cores to use.

parallelFolds

compute folds in parallel or use cores to finish single folds faster. parallelFolds will use folds times as much memory.

tol

Objective tolerance for each fold's refit, by default 1e-5 on a stan fit. On a julia fit, by default a fold stops once a step is predicted to gain less than 1e-4 in log likelihood, which keeps the error in each held-out subject's log likelihood to about 0.014 times the square root of its influence (see casewiseApproximation).

subjectwise

drop random subjects instead of data rows? With method = 'psis', TRUE (the default there) leaves out one subject or group at a time, and FALSE one row at a time.

keepfirstobs

do not drop first observation (more stable estimates)

leaveOutN

if a positive integer is given, the folds argument is ignored and instead the folds are calculated by leaving out every Nth row from the data when fitting. Leaving 2 out would result in 3 folds (starting at rows 1,2,3), each containing one third of the data.

refit

if FALSE, do not optimise parameters for the new data set, just compute the likelihoods etc from the original parameters

casewiseApproximation

TRUE replaces each fold's refit by one Newton step from the full data estimate, which is much faster and close to a refit when no fold moves the estimate far. On a julia fit each fold's influence, the squared length of the step in posterior standard deviations, is returned in foldinfluence. A number instead of TRUE steps only the folds whose influence is below it, and refits the rest. Needs an optimised fit with a covariance. On a stan fit only subject folds and TRUE or FALSE are possible.

method

'kfold' (the default) refits the model once per fold. 'psis' is Pareto smoothed importance sampling leave-one-out without refitting, for backend = 'julia' fits (see Details). It needs the loo package, and refuses the K fold arguments folds, parallelFolds, tol, keepfirstobs, leaveOutN, refit and casewiseApproximation.

nsamples

Number of importance sampling draws for method = 'psis'. For a sampled fit, its posterior draws are used instead, all of them, or thinned to nsamples if it is given. With too few draws the Pareto k of a heavy tailed correction is estimated too low.

Value

For method = 'kfold', a list with foldrows, foldpars, insampleLogLikRow, LogLikRowFolds, outsampleLogLikRow, insampleLogLik, outsampleLogLik, entropy and standard deviation summaries, and processes, whether the folds ran in worker processes. When a julia fit's folds are refitted, foldoptim has a row per fold, with method ('refit' or 'step'), and for a refit the optimiser's iterations, gradients, converged, gain (the predicted gain in log likelihood still left when it stopped) and seconds. A warning counts the refits that stopped without converging. With casewiseApproximation, foldinfluence and foldstepped give each fold's influence and whether it was stepped. scoring is added whenever folds were refitted, saying what was scored (see Details). An intoverpop = 'laplace' fit also adds insampleLogLikSubject and outsampleLogLikSubject. For method = 'psis', an object of class ctLOOpsis, with elpd_loo, se_elpd_loo, p_loo, looic, pointwise (a data frame of elpd_loo, lpd, p_loo and pareto_k per subject, group or row, and refined when leaving out subjects or groups), n_high_k, ndraws, ndropped, proposal_k (the Pareto k of the correction from the normal approximation to the posterior: one value when leaving out subjects or groups, NA for a sampled fit, and one per subject when leaving out rows), level and note.

Details

Works for both backends. On julia, a held-out row is treated as missing, so the filter passes through it without an update or a likelihood contribution. For julia fits, parallelFolds = TRUE runs up to cores folds at once, each in a background R session with its own Julia session, started before the first fold. This needs the future package. The sessions stay open for the next call, and ctJuliaKill('workers') ends them. Without it the folds run one at a time on cores threads. Separate processes are usually faster, except when each fold takes only seconds. $processes on the result says which was used.

Each fold is a separate optimisation, so on a weakly identified model, or one where leaving out a fold leaves a parameter poorly determined, two folds (or the two backends) can end at noticeably different raw parameters with similar likelihoods.

K fold on an intoverpop = 'laplace' fit. The random effects are integrated out, so what is scored depends on the type of fold. With row folds, a held-out row is scored with each subject's random effects at their mode given the fold's training rows, at the fold's parameters. With subject folds, the out-of-sample quantity is each held-out subject's Laplace marginal likelihood at the fold's parameters, returned as outsampleLogLikSubject, and outsampleLogLikRow is NA, because the marginal likelihood does not split into rows. In a multilevel model, a subject's marginal likelihood is conditional on the rest of its outermost group, and subjects of one group held out together share it evenly. insampleLogLik is the Laplace marginal likelihood at the estimate for subject folds, and the sum over rows at the full data modes for row folds.

casewiseApproximation. Each fold's refit is replaced by one Newton step from the full data estimate, est - V %*% s, where s is the score of the held-out data at the estimate and V the inverse of the negative Hessian there. This is the one-step (infinitesimal jackknife) approximation to the refit, and its error grows faster than the step. A fold's influence, t(s) %*% V %*% s, is the squared length of the step in posterior standard deviations. Given a number, folds with an influence at or above it are refitted, so the approximation is used only where the step is short. foldstepped says which folds were stepped. On a julia fit a stepped fold scores only its held-out rows, so its column of LogLikRowFolds is NA elsewhere.

method = 'psis'. Pareto smoothed importance sampling (Vehtari, Gelman and Gabry, 2017), without refitting. It estimates the Bayesian leave-one-out predictive density, a subject's likelihood averaged over the posterior without it. K fold instead scores each fold at its refitted estimate, so the two can differ, most for a subject that moves the estimate. There are two levels:

  • subjectwise = TRUE: leave out one subject at a time, or in a multilevel model one group at a time, since subjects that share a group effect are not independent. Each subject's or group's likelihood has its random effects integrated out, by the Kalman filter under intoverpop = 'augmented' and by the Laplace approximation otherwise. On a sampled fit (optimize = FALSE, or ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample')) the population parameters are its posterior draws. On an optimised fit they are drawn from its normal approximation (fit$estimate$cov, so the fit must have one), widened by a factor of 1.5, and importance weighted to the posterior. A subject or group with a Pareto k above 0.7 is estimated again with nsamples more draws, centred where leaving it out moves the estimate, and the estimate with the lower k is kept (pointwise$refined). This is not done for a fit sampled jointly over parameters and random effects (intoverpop = 'none'). When the normal approximation itself is poor (proposal_k above 0.7), every estimate is unreliable, and a warning says to sample the fit and use its draws. Even without a warning, k is estimated too low from few draws, so a value near 0.7, or a posterior you expect to be skewed (an outlying subject, a variance near zero, binary indicators), is worth rerunning with larger nsamples or on a sampled fit.

  • subjectwise = FALSE, on an optimised intoverpop = 'laplace' fit only: leave out one row at a time, conditional on the estimated population parameters, with each subject's random effects drawn from the normal distribution the Laplace approximation fits at their mode, widened by a factor of 1.5. This is leave-one-out of each row's density given the rows before it, which is not exact time series leave-one-out, and it ignores uncertainty in the population parameters.

Draws for which the random effects' mode cannot be found are dropped and counted. A Pareto k above 0.7 marks an unreliable estimate for that subject, group or row, for which K fold is the better tool.

Laplace fits refined by quadrature. Both methods cross-validate the Laplace approximation, so for a fit refined with intoverpop = 'quadrature' (in ctFit or ctFitUncertainty) they start from the Laplace estimate, fit$laplace$correction$laplace_estimate, and the folds are not refined. scoring says so.

Fold refits are not checked. Each refitted fold skips the final convergence check and Hessian of a full fit (optimcontrol$certify = FALSE), which would cost each fold a Hessian. scoring notes this whenever folds are refitted.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A. and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing, 27, 1413–1432.

Examples

# \donttest{
ctLOO(ctstantestfit)
# }
